stem: When teaching recipient hand-hygiene practices after transplantation, which meal-related timing aligns with standard infection-prevention references?

options.text: Hand-washing before food preparation is optional for immunosuppressed recipients
Meal preparation requires gloves only and never hand-washing
Hand-washing before meals applies only in the hospital, not at home

explanation.rationale_correct: Recipient hand-hygiene teaching includes washing hands before preparing meals and before and after eating, along with washing after bathroom use and animal contact.

rationale_incorrect.B: Hand-washing before preparing meals is specifically recommended rather than optional.
rationale_incorrect.C: Hand-washing with soap and water is emphasized rather than relying on gloves alone without hand hygiene.
rationale_incorrect.D: Home infection-prevention teaching includes meal-related hand-washing rather than limiting it to inpatient care.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 3, Patient Education → e. Infection prevention → i. Hand hygiene

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 3 → e. Infection prevention → i. Hand hygiene (wash hands before preparing meals); PDF p. 115 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Meal-preparation hand-hygiene timing angle distinct from bathroom hand-washing (cctc-1154) and general best-practice item (cctc-1019); anchor verified on Cupples p. 115.

stem: When reinforcing home infection-prevention teaching, which hand-hygiene step aligns with standard references after gardening or handling soil?

options.text: Wash hands after touching plants and soil
Soil contact never requires hand-washing if gloves were worn briefly
Gardening eliminates the need for any hand hygiene afterward
Only hospital staff must wash hands after soil contact, not recipients

explanation.rationale_correct: Recipient hand-hygiene teaching includes washing hands after touching plants and soil, along with washing after animal contact and items that may have contacted feces.

rationale_incorrect.B: Hand-washing after plants and soil is specifically recommended regardless of brief glove use.
rationale_incorrect.C: Gardening increases exposure risk and still requires hand hygiene afterward.
rationale_incorrect.D: Recipients themselves should wash hands after soil contact rather than delegating hygiene to staff only.

stem: A pediatric solid-organ transplant recipient lives with an infant sibling in diapers. Which infection-prevention teaching point aligns with standard references?

options.text: It is preferable that another individual change diapers rather than the pediatric recipient
The immunosuppressed pediatric recipient must always be the primary diaper changer
Diaper changing never poses infection risk to transplant recipients
Diaper hygiene guidance applies only to adult recipients, not children

explanation.rationale_correct: Hand-hygiene teaching notes that after changing diapers it is preferable that another individual change diapers rather than the patient, recognizing fecal exposure risk in immunosuppressed recipients.

rationale_incorrect.B: Another caregiver is preferred for diaper changes rather than requiring the recipient to perform them.
rationale_incorrect.C: Diaper contact is among exposures that warrant infection-prevention precautions.
rationale_incorrect.D: Diaper-related guidance applies to pediatric recipients as well as adults in the household.

stem: A coordinator is updating recipient hand-hygiene teaching. Evaluate the following statements:

elements.text: Recipients should wash hands before preparing meals.
Recipients should wash hands after touching plants and soil.
Antibacterial gel may be used when hands are not visibly soiled and soap and water are unavailable.
Hand-washing after animal contact is unnecessary for transplant recipients.

explanation.rationale_correct: Meal-preparation hand-washing, post-soil hand-washing, and use of antibacterial gel when soap and water are unavailable are supported. Statement IV is false because hand-washing after animal contact is specifically recommended.

rationale_incorrect.A: Statement III is also true—antibacterial gel may supplement hand hygiene when soap and water are unavailable.
rationale_incorrect.C: Statement I is also true; statement IV is false.
rationale_incorrect.D: Statement IV is false because animal-contact hand-washing remains recommended.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 3, Patient Education → e. Infection prevention → i. Hand hygiene
primary_anchor.quote_hint: Before preparing meals … After touching plants and soil … Carry antibacterial gel … After contact with animals
